steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect the power supply to the dishwasher.

steps.title: E9 behavior
steps.body: E9 logs when any button is held longer than 30 seconds.
steps.sourceExcerpt: when some buttons have been pressed over 30 seconds, the dishwasher will warning for E9.

steps.title: Continue procedure
steps.body: Service test mode entered. Continue with component checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: After service test entry, proceed with OEM component test steps.

steps.title: Control panel / touchpad
steps.body: Inspect control panel for stuck, damaged, or moisture-swollen keys. Disconnect power and verify keys release freely.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect control panel for stuck, damaged, or moisture-swollen keys. Disconnect power and verify keys release freely.

steps.title: Retest operation
steps.body: Restore power. Press each touchpad key briefly — none should hold continuously.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Restore power. Press each touchpad key briefly — none should hold continuously.

steps.title: Replace control panel
steps.body: Replace control panel assembly (UI board is bonded to panel).

steps.title: Control panel verified
steps.body: No stuck keys — E9 should not return.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect the power supply to the dishwasher.

steps.title: Ed behavior
steps.body: Ed logs when the display board cannot receive or the main board cannot send for more than 20 seconds.
steps.sourceExcerpt: when the display board cant receive or the main board can't send signal over 20 seconds

steps.title: CN2 display harness seated
steps.body: Remove control panel. Is CN2 (display board) fully seated with no bent pins?
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove control panel. Is CN2 (display board) fully seated with no bent pins?

steps.title: CN2 harness continuity
steps.body: With power off, verify continuity on harness between main PCB CN2 and display PCB (no opens).
steps.sourceExcerpt: With power off, verify continuity on harness between main PCB CN2 and display PCB (no opens).

steps.title: Reseat and retest
steps.body: Reseat CN2 and cycle progress indicator harness; restore power and verify display responds.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reseat CN2 and cycle progress indicator harness; restore power and verify display responds.

steps.title: Replace display or PCB
steps.body: Replace display assembly or main PCB per failed path.

steps.title: Communication verified
steps.body: CN2 path OK — Ed should not return.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect the power supply to the dishwasher.

steps.title: E8 behavior
steps.body: E8 = diverter valve assembly problem. Poor top-rack wash is a common complaint when diverter fails.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Diverter valve assembly problem

steps.title: Continue procedure
steps.body: Service test mode entered. Continue with component checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: After service test entry, proceed with OEM component test steps.

steps.title: Access diverter
steps.body: Remove sump diverter valve cover and storm wash pipe (3 screws). Diverter motor mounts to sump with 2 screws. CN3 carries turbidity and diverter valve detection.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove sump diverter valve cover and storm wash pipe (3 screws). Diverter motor mounts to sump with 2 screws. CN3 carries turbidity and diverter valve detection.

steps.title: Diverter motor and linkage
steps.body: Does diverter motor rotate and change spray path when commanded in service test? Linkage free of debris?
steps.sourceExcerpt: Does diverter motor rotate and change spray path when commanded in service test? Linkage free of debris?

steps.title: Diverter micro switch (CN3)
steps.body: With power off, verify diverter position micro-switch at CN3 toggles with motor travel (no stuck position).
steps.sourceExcerpt: With power off, verify diverter position micro-switch at CN3 toggles with motor travel (no stuck position).

steps.title: CN3 harness
steps.body: Inspect CN3 harness between PCB and diverter detection circuit. Repair opens before replacing PCB.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect CN3 harness between PCB and diverter detection circuit. Repair opens before replacing PCB.

steps.title: Replace diverter motor
steps.body: Replace diverter valve motor on sump.

steps.title: Replace diverter assembly
steps.body: Replace diverter motor and/or micro-switch assembly.

steps.title: Diverter verified
steps.body: Motor and position detection OK — E8 should not return.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect the power supply to the dishwasher.

steps.title: Access drain pump
steps.body: Lay dishwasher on back after removing from installation. Remove base cover screw. Rotate pump 1/4-turn counterclockwise to remove; disconnect 2 wires.
steps.sourceExcerpt: The drain pump has an approximate resistance value of 25- 350.

steps.title: Drain pump winding resistance
steps.body: Measure across drain pump motor terminals. Expect 25–35 Ω.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure across drain pump motor terminals. Expect 25–35 Ω.

steps.title: Check valve and O-ring
steps.body: Verify check valve flapper moves freely and O-ring retained in pump seal before reassembly.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Verify check valve flapper moves freely and O-ring retained in pump seal before reassembly.

steps.title: Replace drain pump
steps.body: Replace drain pump assembly; verify O-ring and clamp.

steps.title: Drain pump verified
steps.body: Pump ohms in spec and check valve OK.

source.manualTitle: Insignia NS-DWR3SS1 Top Control Dishwasher Service Manual

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect the power supply to the dishwasher.

steps.title: E3 behavior
steps.body: E3 logs when water temperature cannot reach the defined value within 90 minutes.
steps.sourceExcerpt: when the temperature cant reached the defined value after 90 minutes, the dishwasher will warning for E3.

steps.title: Continue procedure
steps.body: Service test mode entered. Continue with component checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: After service test entry, proceed with OEM component test steps.

steps.title: Access heating element
steps.body: Remove bottom rack. Lay unit on back; remove base cover. Pull down nylon terminal covers and disconnect heater wires at PO1/PO2.
steps.sourceExcerpt: The heater has an approximate resistance value of 10-1s n

steps.title: Heater element resistance
steps.body: Measure across heating element terminals. Expect 10–15 Ω.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure across heating element terminals. Expect 10–15 Ω.

steps.title: Thermistor follow-up
steps.body: If E3 persists with good heater ohms, run tub thermistor test (nsdwr3ss1-tub-thermistor) and inspect PCB heater output.
steps.sourceExcerpt: If E3 persists with good heater ohms, run tub thermistor test (nsdwr3ss1-tub-thermistor) and inspect PCB heater output.

steps.title: Replace heater
steps.body: Replace heating element; ensure O-ring retained at sump.

steps.title: Heater verified
steps.body: Heater 10–15 Ω — verify thermistor and control if E3 remains.

procedures.title: E1 — Water inlet failure (4 min fill)

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect the power supply to the dishwasher.

steps.title: E1 behavior
steps.body: E1 logs when the flow meter cannot detect defined water within 4 minutes during the inlet step. OCR may show El — treat as E1.
steps.sourceExcerpt: If the flow meter can't detect the defined water after 4 minutes, the dishwasher will warning for E1.

steps.title: Water supply and installation
steps.body: Verify supply valve on, adequate pressure, inlet screen clean, drain hose not siphoning, and dishwasher level.
steps.sourceExcerpt: 1. check the water supply

steps.title: Bench fill path
steps.body: Power off. Access kick panel. Inspect CON3 inlet harness, flow meter at CN4, pressure switch hose, and drain path. Run fill-valve ohms test (nsdwr3ss1-fill-valve) and drain pump test if sump retains water.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Access kick panel. Inspect CON3 inlet harness, flow meter at CN4, pressure switch hose, and drain path. Run fill-valve ohms test (nsdwr3ss1-fill-valve) and drain pump test if sump retains water.

steps.title: Pressure switch hose and tubing
steps.body: Pressure switch hose runs from switch to sump via air breaker. Hose kinked, disconnected, or blocked?
steps.sourceExcerpt: 5. check the pressure switch

steps.title: Flow meter and CN4
steps.body: Inspect CN4 flow meter / flood detection harness for damage or poor connection at main PCB.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect CN4 flow meter / flood detection harness for damage or poor connection at main PCB.

steps.title: Correct supply issue
steps.body: Restore water supply, correct installation, and retest fill.

steps.title: Repair pressure switch path
steps.body: Repair or replace pressure switch hose; verify switch seated in base bracket.

steps.title: Fill path verified
steps.body: Supply, inlet valve, flow meter, pressure switch, and drain prerequisites checked — retest for E1.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect the power supply to the dishwasher.

steps.title: E4 behavior
steps.body: E4 logs when water floods the bottom pan and the detective micro-switch moves.
steps.sourceExcerpt: the water flood into the bottom and result in the detective switch moves, the dishwasher will warning for E4.

steps.title: Detergent, level, and leak source
steps.body: Check detergent type/amount, appliance level, and visible leak at door gasket, sump, or hoses.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check detergent type/amount, appliance level, and visible leak at door gasket, sump, or hoses.

steps.title: CN4 flood detection
steps.body: Inspect CN4 rinse-aid / flow meter / water-flood detection harness and base pan micro-switch.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect CN4 rinse-aid / flow meter / water-flood detection harness and base pan micro-switch.

steps.title: Drain pan and pump
steps.body: Remove standing water from base. Does drain pump run and remove water when commanded?
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove standing water from base. Does drain pump run and remove water when commanded?

steps.title: Locate leak
steps.body: With pan dry, run a short fill cycle and inspect sump, door seal, air breaker, and hose clamps for leak source.
steps.sourceExcerpt: With pan dry, run a short fill cycle and inspect sump, door seal, air breaker, and hose clamps for leak source.

steps.title: Drain pump bench test
steps.body: Run nsdwr3ss1-drain-pump for 25–35 Ω winding check and check valve.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Run nsdwr3ss1-drain-pump for 25–35 Ω winding check and check valve.

steps.title: Correct installation
steps.body: Reduce detergent, level unit, or repair identified leak source.

steps.title: Service drain path
steps.body: Replace drain pump or clear obstruction; dry base pan before retest.

steps.title: Overflow path checked
steps.body: Pan dry, flood switch reset, drain verified — retest for E4.

source.manualTitle: Insignia NS-DWR3SS1 Top Control Dishwasher Service Manual

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect the power supply to the dishwasher.

steps.title: E6 / E7 behavior
steps.body: E6 = NTC open (thermal sensor cut). E7 = NTC short. Both may appear in factory mode; also affects E3 heat path.
steps.sourceExcerpt: E6 - thermal sensor cut. E7 - thermal sensor short.

steps.title: Access tub thermistor
steps.body: Lay dishwasher on back; remove base cover. Thermistor on back of sump — disconnect harness before ohms.

steps.title: Tub thermistor resistance
steps.body: Measure at room temperature (~25°C). Expect 10 kΩ ±2%.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure at room temperature (~25°C). Expect 10 kΩ ±2%.

steps.title: Harness check
steps.body: Inspect thermistor harness for pin damage at PCB and sump. Repair opens before replacing PCB.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect thermistor harness for pin damage at PCB and sump. Repair opens before replacing PCB.

steps.title: Replace thermistor
steps.body: Replace tub thermistor; retain O-ring at sump.

steps.title: Thermistor verified
steps.body: NTC in spec — if E6/E7/E3 persist, suspect PCB.
